--- title: Linting description: Check text blocks with your own rules, underline findings by severity, and fix them from a popover or a list. docs: - route: /docs/components/lint title: Lint Component - route: /docs/examples/lint title: Lint Demo --- ## Features - Checks only the text blocks a commit changed, and calls each rule once per changed block. - Reads a block's text through inline elements and leaves out non-content text, such as struck suggestions. - Paints findings as decorations, so nothing is written into the document or its history. - Lists findings in document order, and rebuilds the list only after findings change or blocks move. - Applies a fix as its own undo step, and refuses a finding whose text has changed. - Keeps a server reply only while its block matches the one it sent, marks and properties included. - Moves between findings with `F8` and `Shift+F8` in the kit. ## Kit Usage ### Installation ```bash npx shadcn@latest add @plate/lint ``` ### Add Kit ```tsx import { createEditor } from 'platejs/react'; import { LintKit } from '@/components/editor/lint'; const editor = createEditor({ plugins: [ // ...otherPlugins, ...LintKit, ], }); ``` `LintKit` configures `BaseLintPlugin` with two example rules, `fillerWords` and `commaSpacing`, underline classes per severity, the `F8` and `Shift+F8` keys and `LintPopover`. The same file exports `useLintFindings` and `useLintFindingAt` for your own lint UI. ## Rules A rule checks one text block. `check` receives the block's content text and returns matches with UTF-16 offsets into that text, a message and optional fixes. It also receives the block and the editor, so a rule can skip code: ```ts import { BaseCodeBlockPlugin, type Editor, type Element } from 'platejs'; import type { LintRule } from 'platejs/lint'; const isProse = (editor: Editor, block: Element) => { const codeBlock = editor.plugin(BaseCodeBlockPlugin); return !codeBlock.installed || block.type !== codeBlock.schema.type; }; export const commaSpacing: LintRule = { id: 'style/comma-spacing', severity: 'error', check: (text, { block, editor }) => isProse(editor, block) ? Array.from(text.matchAll(/ , ?/g), (match) => ({ start: match.index, end: match.index + match[0].length, message: 'Remove the space before commas.', fixes: [', '], })) : [], }; ``` `severity` is `'error'`, `'warning'` or `'info'`. The plugin drops a match whose offsets are not integers inside the text, or that selects nothing. When a rule throws, the block keeps the findings of its other rules and the store's `error` holds the failure. Set the rules through `initialState`, or pass new rules to `api.run`: ```ts editor.plugin(BaseLintPlugin).api.run([commaSpacing, fillerWords]); ``` ## Server rules A rule whose `check` returns a promise is a server rule. Abort the request through `signal`: ```ts const terminology: LintRule = { id: 'server/terminology', severity: 'info', check: async (text, { signal }) => { const response = await fetch('/api/lint', { body: JSON.stringify({ text }), method: 'POST', signal, }); return response.json(); }, }; ``` The plugin keeps a reply only while the block matches the one it sent, including its type, marks and inline elements. When the block changes before the reply arrives, the plugin drops the reply and sends the latest block, even when the old request failed. Typing in a block hides that block's server findings until the reply for its new text arrives. Each block and rule has at most one request in flight, and each rule at most four. The rest wait, and a block whose text changed since its last request goes ahead of blocks not checked yet. `clear`, `run` and removing the block abort the request through `signal`. A rejected request sets the store's `error`. ## Findings list `api.findings()` returns the findings in document order, as the same array until the store's `version` moves. Subscribe to the store to read it in React: ```tsx import { BaseLintPlugin } from 'platejs/lint'; import { useEditor } from 'platejs/react'; import * as React from 'react'; export function useLintFindings() { const lint = useEditor().plugin(BaseLintPlugin); return React.useSyncExternalStore( lint.store.subscribe, lint.api.findings, lint.api.findings ); } ``` A finding holds its `id`, `ruleId`, `severity`, `message`, matched `text` and `fixes`, with no offsets. Pass its `id` to `select` or `fix`: ```tsx function LintList() { const lint = useEditor().plugin(BaseLintPlugin); const findings = useLintFindings(); return (
    {findings.slice(0, 50).map((finding) => (
  1. {finding.fixes.length > 0 && ( )}
    2. ))}
); } ``` Ids survive an edit in the same block that leaves its findings unchanged, such as typing before a finding. Any other change to the block's findings, from an edit or a server reply, gives all of them new ids, and `fix` and `select` return `false` for an old one. ## Collaboration and suggestions A collaborator's edit commits like a local one, so the plugin re-checks each block it changes. In a suggesting editor, a fix becomes a suggestion like any other edit. The replaced text stays as a struck suggestion that rules never see, and the inserted fix counts as content. ## Caret popover `useLintFindingAt` returns the finding under the selection focus. It reads again after store changes and commits, so a server reply that lands under a still caret opens `LintPopover`: ```tsx export function useLintFindingAt() { const editor = useEditor(); const lint = editor.plugin(BaseLintPlugin); const subscribe = React.useCallback( (onChange: () => void) => { const offStore = lint.store.subscribe(onChange); const offCommit = editor.subscribeCommit(onChange); return () => { offStore(); offCommit(); }; }, [editor, lint] ); return React.useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, lint.api.at, lint.api.at); } ``` `LintPopover` opens while the editor is focused and editable. It shows the message, the rule id, one button per fix and **Fix and next**, which applies the first fix and selects the next finding. Its buttons keep focus in the editor, so typing continues after the fixed text. ## Keyboard behavior | Key | Behavior | | --- | --- | | `F8` | Select the next finding, wrapping to the first. | | `Shift+F8` | Select the previous finding, wrapping to the last. | When findings overlap, `F8` and the popover reach the first one. ## Manual Usage Use the headless plugin without the copied UI: ```ts import { createEditor } from 'platejs'; import { BaseLintPlugin } from 'platejs/lint'; const editor = createEditor({ initialValue, plugins: [ BaseLintPlugin.configure({ initialState: { rules: [commaSpacing] } }), ], }); const lint = editor.plugin(BaseLintPlugin); const [first] = lint.api.findings(); if (first) lint.update.fix(first.id); ``` In React, lift it with `toReactPlugin` and style its decorations through `decorate.attributes`. Each decoration carries `data-lint-id`, `data-lint-rule` and `data-lint-severity`: ```tsx import { BaseLintPlugin } from 'platejs/lint'; import { toReactPlugin } from 'platejs/react'; const LintPlugin = toReactPlugin(BaseLintPlugin).configure({ initialState: { rules: [commaSpacing] }, decorate: { attributes: { className: 'underline decoration-wavy data-[lint-severity=error]:decoration-destructive', }, }, }); ``` The plugin checks the main document only, not text in nested editable areas inside blocks. ## Plugins ### `BaseLintPlugin` The rules to run. Default: `[]`. Whether the plugin lints. `clear` sets it to `false` and `run` to `true`. Default: `true`. The store also holds `version`, which moves whenever the findings list changes, and `error`, the last rule failure. ## API Reference ### `api.findings` Findings in document order, the same array until `version` moves. Empty while the plugin is cleared. ### `api.at` The finding under the selection focus, read from its block alone. ### `api.run` Lint the whole document again and repaint. Rules that replace the current ones. ### `api.clear` Stop linting, drop every finding and abort server requests until the next `run`. ### `update.fix` Replace a finding's text with one of its fixes, as its own undo step. The finding's id. The fix to apply. Default: `0`. Whether the fix was applied. `false` when the finding or the fix is gone. ### `update.select` The finding to select. Whether the finding still exists and was selected. ### `update.move` Select the previous or next finding from the selection, wrapping. Whether a finding was selected. ### `LintRule` The rule's id, copied to each finding as `ruleId`. The severity of the rule's findings. Checks one block's content text. Each `LintMatch` is `{ start, end, message, fixes? }`, with UTF-16 offsets into `text`. ## Related docs - [Find](/docs/plate/find) - [Plugin Shortcuts](/docs/plate/plugin-shortcuts) - [Authored Changes](/docs/plate/authored-changes)
